authors: Qingqing Zhao, Chu-Ren Huang, and Kathleen Ahrens
title: Directionality of linguistic synesthesia in Mandarin: A corpus-based study
reading_scope: publisher abstract and university repository metadata/abstract; not full methods
supportable_claim: Mandarin corpus mappings showed unidirectional, biased-directional and bidirectional patterns, challenging a universal sensory-transfer hierarchy.
limitation: Linguistic usage does not identify perceptual synesthesia or demonstrate a neural mechanism.

authors: Mai Mori and Kimi Akita
title: The Meanings of Synesthetic Metaphors Closely Align With Crossmodal Correspondences
reading_scope: publisher full-text methods, results and discussion inspected
supportable_claim: Ratings for sensory metaphors and imagined crossmodal correspondences generally aligned, with conventionality and emotional scales modifying the relationship.
limitation: Two independent groups of 90 English monolingual US participants rated language prompts; sensory correspondences were elicited through imagination rather than actual tastants, tones or visual stimuli. Correlation does not settle causal direction.

authors: Julia Simner
title: Defining synaesthesia
reading_scope: author accepted manuscript abstract, introduction and selected definitional sections
supportable_claim: Definitions limited to merging sensory modalities omit conceptual or linguistic inducers and the heterogeneity of synesthetic experiences.
limitation: A definitional argument rather than proof of a single mechanism; disputed criteria must not be presented as necessary and sufficient diagnostic rules.

authors: David M. Eagleman, Arielle D. Kagan, Stephanie S. Nelson, Deepak Sagaram, and Anand K. Sarma
title: A standardized test battery for the study of synesthesia
reading_scope: PubMed abstract, metadata and author-hosted PDF selected methods
supportable_claim: Behavioral research operationalizes features such as repeated inducer-concurrent consistency and speeded congruency, instead of inferring synesthesia from vivid metaphors alone.
limitation: This battery targets specific forms; consistency or a personal learning narrative alone is not evidence for every form of synesthesia or a learning mechanism.

authors: Charles Spence
title: Crossmodal correspondences: A tutorial review
reading_scope: publisher and PubMed abstracts plus selected conceptual material
supportable_claim: Crossmodal correspondences concern systematic compatibility between sensory features and can constrain binding alongside spatial, temporal and semantic relations.
limitation: Compatibility is not identical to perceptual synesthesia or universal one-to-one translation.

authors: Marc O. Ernst and Martin S. Banks
title: Humans integrate visual and haptic information in a statistically optimal fashion
reading_scope: publisher abstract and metadata; institution-hosted PDF attempted but extracted text corrupted, not counted as a full-text read
supportable_claim: Human visual-haptic height estimates in the tested task closely followed reliability-weighted cue integration predictions.
limitation: A bounded estimation task; it does not prove optimal fusion across all modalities, correlated errors, tasks or architectures.

authors: Konrad P. Körding, Ulrik Beierholm, Wei Ji Ma, Steven Quartz, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, and Ladan Shams
title: Causal Inference in Multisensory Perception
reading_scope: publisher abstract and selected model/task descriptions
supportable_claim: An observer model that infers common versus separate causes predicts nonlinear audiovisual localization behavior.
limitation: Perceptual common-source inference is not intervention-based causal identification of physical dynamics.

authors: Aaron R. Seitz, Robyn Kim, and Ladan Shams
title: Sound facilitates visual learning
reading_scope: PubMed abstract and author-hosted PDF results, training procedure and silent-transfer control
supportable_claim: Audiovisual training accelerated learning of visual motion compared with visual training across ten days while matching visual-signal exposure; silent testing supported transfer beyond concurrent auditory cues.
limitation: A small, task-specific study of nonsynesthetic multisensory learning, not a broad intelligence effect. Final trained-direction group differences were not significant after both groups approached asymptote.

authors: Nicolas Rothen and Beat Meier
title: Do Synesthetes Have a General Advantage in Visual Search and Episodic Memory? A Case for Group Studies
reading_scope: publisher full-text methods, results and discussion
supportable_claim: Thirteen grapheme-color synesthetes and matched controls showed no significant group advantage in the tested search and digit-matrix memory tasks.
limitation: Small sample and narrow tasks; null results do not establish absence of all benefits or equivalence across the population.

authors: Katrin Lunke and Beat Meier
title: New insights into mechanisms of enhanced synaesthetic memory: Benefits are synaesthesia-type-specific
reading_scope: publisher abstract, methods, subgroup results and discussion
supportable_claim: Across 97 synesthetes in four groups and matched controls, recognition results included a small overall advantage and subtype-by-stimulus differences.
limitation: Not randomized synesthesia assignment or a test of general learning. Specific advantages differed across colors, music and words; several subgroup comparisons were inconclusive.

authors: Charles Spence and Nicola Di Stefano
title: Sensory translation between audition and vision
evidence_type: narrative historical review; close related work
reading_scope: publisher abstract, terminology passages and conclusion; no experimental replication
supportable_claim: Prior work already compares sensory translation, synesthesia, metaphors and crossmodal associations; meaningful translation need not imply a universal literal mapping.
limitation: Historical/theoretical synthesis, not proof of an amodal code or AI performance benefit.

authors: Kaiyu Qiu, Zixiu Jiang, Ke Jiang, and Huilin Qiu
title: From multisensory integration to synaesthesia: a boundary-preserving continuum and research framework
evidence_type: hypothesis and theory article; close related work
reading_scope: publisher metadata, abstract, introduction and outline
supportable_claim: An existing conceptual framework distinguishes ordinary integration, correspondences, cultural metaphors and synesthesia without collapsing their evidential boundaries.
limitation: Proposed heuristic continuum, not experimentally established developmental ladder, biological mechanism or AI equivalence.

authors: Han Xiao and Thomas Stibor
title: Toward Artificial Synesthesia: Linking Images and Sounds via Words
publication: NIPS Workshop on Machine Learning for Next Generation Computer Vision Challenges
evidence_type: Workshop modeling and prototype study; historical precedent
reading_scope: Primary PDF title page, abstract, introduction, model formulation; landing-page metadata compared. Not independently reproduced.
bounded_claim: Uses text-mediated probabilistic association to link images and sounds; establishes prior use of artificial synesthesia terminology and a crossmodal bridge concept.
limits: Association and human-judged plausibility are not measurements of machine experience, exact physical inference, or broad learning superiority. Landing page says Frederic Stumpf; primary PDF says Thomas Stibor, used here.

authors: Jiquan Ngiam, Aditya Khosla, Mingyu Kim, Juhan Nam, Honglak Lee, and Andrew Y. Ng
title: Multimodal Deep Learning
publication: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Machine Learning, pp. 689-696
reading_scope: Primary PDF abstract, learning-setting definitions, architectures, and experimental setup through section 4.2. No code run.
bounded_claim: Distinguishes multimodal fusion, multimodal pretraining followed by single-modality use, and training/testing a classifier on different modalities; reports audio-visual speech evidence.
limits: Bounded speech datasets and preprocessing; crossmodal feature transfer is not arbitrary physical state reconstruction or subjective synesthesia.

authors: Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Chris Hallacy, Aditya Ramesh, Gabriel Goh, Sandhini Agarwal, Girish Sastry, Amanda Askell, Pamela Mishkin, Jack Clark, Gretchen Krueger, and Ilya Sutskever
title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
publication: Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, pp. 8748-8763
reading_scope: PMLR metadata and abstract; indexed primary PDF abstract/introduction; arXiv author abstract. No reproduction.
bounded_claim: CLIP learns from image-text pairing and demonstrates zero-shot visual classification transfer across benchmark datasets.
limits: Semantic matching and classification do not establish sensor calibration, action-conditioned physical prediction, or conscious experience.

authors: Rohit Girdhar, Alaaeldin El-Nouby, Zhuang Liu, Mannat Singh, Kalyan Vasudev Alwala, Armand Joulin, and Ishan Misra
title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
publication: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, pp. 15180-15190
reading_scope: CVF abstract and citation metadata; indexed primary PDF introduction and beginning of method. Direct PDF open returned 403; no full-paper-reading claim.
bounded_claim: Binds images, text, audio, depth, thermal, and IMU embeddings using image-paired data; demonstrates emergent crossmodal retrieval and recognition without all modality-pair combinations in training.
limits: Does not show that arbitrary unpaired sensors align, that every pair has task-sufficient shared information, or that embeddings reconstruct calibrated physical quantities.

authors: Yonglong Tian, Dilip Krishnan, and Phillip Isola
title: Contrastive Multiview Coding
reading_scope: Official ECVA abstract and indexed primary PDF abstract; not full text or reproduction.
bounded_claim: Investigates compact representations emphasizing shared information between views and reports improved scene-semantic representations with more views in its evaluated settings.
limits: The reported more-view result is task and data dependent, not a monotonic law of sensor count or a guarantee of preserving unique physical information.

authors: Tadas Baltrusaitis, Chaitanya Ahuja, and Louis-Philippe Morency
title: Multimodal Machine Learning: A Survey and Taxonomy
publication: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 41(2), pp. 423-443; accepted manuscript available in 2018
reading_scope: Author/academic-hosted accepted PDF introduction and representation sections; arXiv abstract; publication metadata corroborated. Not an exhaustive reread.
bounded_claim: Already organizes representation, translation, alignment, fusion, and co-learning; distinguishes joint from coordinated representations.
limits: A survey taxonomy is not empirical proof of universal multisensory benefits. This new review cannot claim to invent these task distinctions.

authors: Paul Pu Liang, Amir Zadeh, and Louis-Philippe Morency
title: Foundations and Trends in Multimodal Machine Learning: Principles, Challenges, and Open Questions
publication: ACM Computing Surveys 56(10), Article 264; author preprint arXiv:2209.03430
reading_scope: Author preprint abstract and metadata; author MIT publication page confirms ACM Computing Surveys 2024. Publisher DOI fetch unavailable; 2024 final full text not read.
bounded_claim: Prior synthesis treats modality heterogeneity, connections and interactions, and six challenges including representation, alignment, reasoning, generation, transference and quantification.
limits: The scope strongly overlaps any broad claim of a new multimodal framework; the contribution here should be cross-field clarification and a bounded evaluation agenda.

authors: Weiyao Wang, Du Tran, and Matt Feiszli
title: What Makes Training Multi-Modal Classification Networks Hard?
publication: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
evidence_type: Peer-reviewed empirical negative-result and optimization study
reading_scope: Indexed primary PDF abstract, introduction, and Table 1; author arXiv abstract. Direct PDF fetch failed. No reproduction.
bounded_claim: In evaluated video-classification settings, naive multimodal training can underperform the strongest single modality; capacity-related overfitting and unequal modality learning dynamics are implicated.
limits: Not evidence that multimodal training is generally inferior; proposed optimization mitigations and task dependence must be retained.

authors: Weixin Liang, Yuhui Zhang, Yongchan Kwon, Serena Yeung, and James Zou
title: Mind the Gap: Understanding the Modality Gap in Multi-modal Contrastive Representation Learning
publication: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35
evidence_type: Peer-reviewed theoretical and empirical representation analysis
reading_scope: Primary PDF abstract/metadata and selected implications excerpt; author project explanation and arXiv abstract. No code run.
bounded_claim: Image and text embeddings can occupy separated regions despite a nominally shared space; initialization and contrastive optimization affect this geometry.
limits: A geometric gap alone does not measure physical understanding or prove an optimal gap is zero. The paper studies task-dependent effects of changing the gap.

authors: Paul Pu Liang, Zihao Deng, Martin Ma, James Zou, Louis-Philippe Morency, and Ruslan Salakhutdinov
title: Factorized Contrastive Learning: Going Beyond Multi-view Redundancy
publication: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
evidence_type: Peer-reviewed theoretical and empirical multimodal representation study
reading_scope: Primary abstract, selected theory/limitations and appendix excerpts; metadata. No independent derivation audit or reproduction.
bounded_claim: When task-relevant information is modality-unique, objectives focused on shared information can be insufficient; FactorCL separately models shared and unique components.
limits: Theoretical claims depend on stated information and augmentation assumptions; not proof all contrastive models necessarily discard every unique feature.

authors: Benoit Dufumier, Javiera Castillo Navarro, Devis Tuia, and Jean-Philippe Thiran
title: What to Align in Multimodal Contrastive Learning?
evidence_type: Peer-reviewed theoretical and empirical study; CoMM
reading_scope: Primary PDF title, abstract, theory assumptions, architecture, training objective and controlled-experiment setup (sections 1-4.1). No reproduction.
bounded_claim: Aligning augmented joint multimodal representations is proposed to preserve shared, unique and synergistic information; evaluated with controlled and real-world tasks.
limits: Theory uses ideal label-preserving augmentation/expressivity/optimization assumptions, with information analysis principally for two modalities. No universal sensor-scale or world-model guarantee.

authors: Paul Pu Liang, Yiwei Lyu, Xiang Fan, Zetian Wu, Yun Cheng, Jason Wu, Leslie Chen, Peter Wu, Michelle A. Lee, Yuke Zhu, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, and Louis-Philippe Morency
title: MultiBench: Multiscale Benchmarks for Multimodal Representation Learning
reading_scope: Author abstract and metadata only; no dataset or code downloaded.
bounded_claim: Provides a precedent for evaluating generalization, time/space cost, and noisy/missing-modality robustness across diverse tasks.
limits: Its existence does not establish any particular proposed model's performance or legal rights to redistribute constituent datasets.

authors: Tristan Thrush, Ryan Jiang, Max Bartolo, Amanpreet Singh, Adina Williams, Douwe Kiela, and Candace Ross
title: Winoground: Probing Vision and Language Models for Visio-Linguistic Compositionality
publication: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, pp. 5238-5248
evidence_type: Peer-reviewed benchmark and empirical failure analysis
reading_scope: CVF abstract and bibliographic metadata; arXiv abstract. Direct PDF fetch failed; no reproduction.
bounded_claim: Image-caption pairing with captions sharing words but changing order exposed failures of the models evaluated in 2022.
limits: Do not generalize the historic model results to all 2026 models or interpret the benchmark as a pure test of syntax; see A14.

authors: Anuj Diwan, Layne Berry, Eunsol Choi, David Harwath, and Kyle Mahowald
title: Why is Winoground Hard? Investigating Failures in Visuolinguistic Compositionality
publication: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pp. 2236-2250
reading_scope: ACL abstract and citation metadata; author arXiv abstract. No reproduction.
bounded_claim: Winoground also demands commonsense reasoning, visual detail localization and multimodal fusion; failures cannot automatically be assigned solely to language compositionality.
limits: Benchmark diagnosis is specific to analyzed data/models; no claim that it exhausts every source of failure.

authors: Yunzhu Li; Jun-Yan Zhu; Russ Tedrake; Antonio Torralba
title: Connecting Touch and Vision via Cross-Modal Prediction
publication: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 10609-10618
evidence_type: Primary empirical conference paper; author manuscript inspected
reading_scope: Primary abstract; author-manuscript selected introduction, dataset, unseen-object evaluation, contact timing, perceptual evaluation and discussion sections. CVF HTML access failed; arXiv PDF inspected.
bounded_claims: Crossmodal vision/touch prediction is established for this dataset; realism and plausible localization do not establish calibrated mechanics, control, or subjective experience.

authors: Michelle A. Lee; Yuke Zhu; Krishnan Srinivasan; Parth Shah; Silvio Savarese; Li Fei-Fei; Animesh Garg; Jeannette Bohg
title: Making Sense of Vision and Touch: Self-Supervised Learning of Multimodal Representations for Contact-Rich Tasks
publication: 2019 International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), 8943-8950
evidence_type: Primary empirical conference paper; author-hosted accepted manuscript
reading_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, modality encoders, self-supervised prediction objectives, controller, experiment setup and modality-ablation passages in the ICRA version. Bibliographic title/author identity checked against IEEE conference awards brochure.
bounded_claims: Vision, force/torque and proprioception representations trained with action-conditional and alignment objectives are evaluated on simulated and physical peg insertion; no general-world-model result.

authors: Hao Li; Yizhi Zhang; Junzhe Zhu; Shaoxiong Wang; Michelle A. Lee; Huazhe Xu; Edward Adelson; Li Fei-Fei; Ruohan Gao; Jiajun Wu
title: See, Hear, and Feel: Smart Sensory Fusion for Robotic Manipulation
publication: Proceedings of the 6th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2022), PMLR 205:1368-1378
reading_scope: PMLR bibliographic record; arXiv HTML 2212.03858v1 main text including data capture, model, baselines, dense packing and bead-pouring experiments, and limitations. PDF retrieval failed or exceeded tool size limit; supplement not inspected.
bounded_claims: Visual, acoustic and tactile fusion improves selected manipulation outcomes relative to reported baselines; modality utility varies by contact configuration, and the system uses human demonstrations and a specialized setup.

authors: Martina Zambelli; Yusuf Aytar; Francesco Visin; Yuxiang Zhou; Raia Hadsell
title: Learning rich touch representations through cross-modal self-supervision
publication: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Robot Learning, PMLR 155:1415-1425
reading_scope: PMLR record; selected primary PDF methods and dataset sections covering touch/proprioceptive encoding, crossmodal objectives and simulated Shadow Hand setup; abstract-level outcome summary. No independent reproduction.
bounded_claims: Crossmodal self-supervision can improve tactile features for reported few-shot tasks in simulation; visual training supervision must be distinguished from visual deployment inputs.

authors: Carolina Higuera; Akash Sharma; Chaithanya Krishna Bodduluri; Taosha Fan; Patrick Lancaster; Mrinal Kalakrishnan; Michael Kaess; Byron Boots; Mike Lambeta; Tingfan Wu; Mustafa Mukadam
title: Sparsh: Self-supervised touch representations for vision-based tactile sensing
publication: Proceedings of the 8th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2024), PMLR 270:885-915
evidence_type: Primary empirical conference paper; abstract-level evidence only
reading_scope: PMLR primary abstract and complete bibliographic record. Full experiments and supplementary material not inspected; no numerical effect estimate reused.
bounded_claims: Self-supervised tactile-only and cross-sensor representations are available as a relevant strong comparator; this source is not evidence of a multimodal advantage.

authors: Martina Zambelli; Antoine Cully; Yiannis Demiris
title: Multimodal representation models for prediction and control from partial information
evidence_type: Primary empirical journal paper; accepted author manuscript
reading_scope: Accepted-manuscript abstract and selected introduction, multimodal architecture, training strategy, sensor definitions and discussion passages. Publisher journal identity checked via primary accepted-version cover page.
bounded_claims: An iCub can use a learned shared representation for missing sensory data, prediction and trajectory imitation in the stated setting; tracked hand coordinates and egocentric-perspective assumptions constrain the result.

authors: Pim de Haan; Dinesh Jayaraman; Sergey Levine
title: Causal Confusion in Imitation Learning
publication: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (NeurIPS 2019)
evidence_type: Primary theoretical and empirical conference paper
reading_scope: Official proceedings abstract; selected primary PDF introduction, causal formulation and benchmark sections including equal-architecture nuisance-feature experiments. Appendix proofs not fully checked; driving references not independently reproduced.
bounded_claims: Additional observational features can reduce closed-loop imitation performance under the reported distribution shifts; held-out demonstration accuracy alone is insufficient.

authors: Andrew Owens; Phillip Isola; Josh McDermott; Antonio Torralba; Edward H. Adelson; William T. Freeman
title: Visually Indicated Sounds
publication: Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2405-2413
evidence_type: Primary empirical conference paper; author manuscript inspected
reading_scope: Author manuscript abstract and selected evaluation/test-split, sound-plausibility, material-classification and normalization passages. CVPR publication year checked against the authors' MIT publication record. No reproduction.
bounded_claims: Video-to-impact-sound prediction captures some material-related regularities, but perceptual realism is not identified physical dynamics; reported test-video statistical normalization must not be overlooked.

authors: Jan C. Willems; Paolo Rapisarda; Ivan Markovsky; Bart L. M. De Moor
title: A note on persistency of excitation
reading_scope: Publisher primary abstract, introduction and theorem-related preview/corollary passages; university author-PDF indexed first page checked for metadata. Direct author-PDF open failed; complete proof not audited.
bounded_claims: Sufficient excitation of a controllable LTI system permits finite trajectory windows to span the system behavior under the paper's assumptions; this is not unrestricted nonlinear identifiability.

authors: J. Arjan G. M. de Visser, Clifford W. Zeyl, Philip J. Gerrish, Jeffrey L. Blanchard, and Richard E. Lenski
title: Diminishing returns from mutation supply rate in asexual populations
reading_scope: PubMed abstract plus university/LTEE publication records; no complete methods read
supportable_claim: Adaptation in tested asexual E. coli populations was proportional to mutation supply only in some population-size/initial-adaptation conditions; returns diminished elsewhere.
limitation: Not a universal species-level proportionality or universal mutation-rate optimum. Mutation supply and per-individual mutation rate are distinct.

authors: Kathleen Sprouffske, José Aguilar-Rodríguez, Paul Sniegowski, and Andreas Wagner
title: High mutation rates limit evolutionary adaptation in Escherichia coli
reading_scope: publisher abstract and indexed experimental-design/results excerpts
supportable_claim: Across four mutation-rate backgrounds followed for 3000 generations, greater diversity did not monotonically improve adaptation: some highest-rate populations adapted less, and their mutation rates fell.
limitation: Asexual laboratory E. coli, selected media and growth-based fitness proxies; not a universal relationship for species adaptability.

authors: Sébastien Wielgoss, Jeffrey E. Barrick, Olivier Tenaillon, Michael J. Wiser, W. James Dittmar, Stéphane Cruveiller, Béatrice Chane-Woon-Ming, Claudine Médigue, Richard E. Lenski, and Dominique Schneider
title: Mutation rate dynamics in a bacterial population reflect tension between adaptation and genetic load
publication: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 110(1), 222-227; online 2012
evidence_type: primary phylogenomic analysis of experimental evolution
reading_scope: publisher abstract, introduction and bibliographic metadata
supportable_claim: A laboratory lineage that had become hypermutable was later invaded by independent lineages with reduced mutation rates, consistent with changing balance between adaptive opportunity and deleterious load.
limitation: One asexual experimental population; genomic-rate inference includes assumptions about synonymous substitutions. This is not evidence of foresighted global optimization.

authors: Jeff Clune, Dusan Misevic, Charles Ofria, Richard E. Lenski, Santiago F. Elena, and Rafael Sanjuán
title: Natural Selection Fails to Optimize Mutation Rates for Long-Term Adaptation on Rugged Fitness Landscapes
reading_scope: publisher abstract and author summary plus indexed results/discussion
supportable_claim: In studied digital organisms, self-evolved mutation rates on rugged landscapes could lie below rates maximizing long-term adaptation; smooth versus rugged controls changed this outcome.
limitation: Avida experiments establish behavior of the specified digital system, not a universal law for organisms or modern neural-network optimizers.

authors: Bhaskar Kumawat, Alexander Lalejini, Monica M. Acosta, and Luis Zaman
title: Evolution takes multiple paths to evolvability when facing environmental change
publication: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 122(1), e2413930121; online 31 December 2024
reading_scope: publisher abstract, significance, selected discussion and data/software availability
supportable_claim: In Avida, environmental change shaped both mutation rates and local genotype-to-phenotype structure, with different contributions to adaptation to recurring and novel environments.
limitation: The reported favorable switching regime is model-specific. It does not establish an optimal ecological timescale or mutation probability for biological species or AI.
